# Quickstart: Normative/Advisory Detection (WI-33)

**Generated by**: `/speckit.plan` | **Date**: 2026-02-17

---

## What Was Built

WI-33 adds modality detection to the FORGE pipeline. After running, every `PolicyRequirement` is tagged with either `Modality::Normative` (mandatory) or `Modality::Advisory` (recommended), and every OSCAL control in the generated output includes a `prop` with `name: "modality"`.

---

## End-to-End Flow

### Input: Mixed-Modality Policy Document

```markdown
# Access Control

- Organizations must implement multi-factor authentication for all privileged accounts.
- Systems shall enforce session timeouts of no more than 30 minutes.
- Organizations should implement logging for all failed authentication attempts.
- Periodic access reviews may be conducted quarterly.
- Encrypt all data at rest using approved algorithms.
```

### Run FORGE

```bash
forge convert policy.md --output catalog.json
```

### Output: OSCAL Catalog JSON (excerpt)

```json
{
  "catalog": {
    "groups": [{
      "id": "access-control",
      "title": "Access Control",
      "controls": [
        {
          "id": "POL-AC-001",
          "title": "Organizations must implement multi-factor authentication...",
          "props": [
            { "name": "modality", "value": "normative" }
          ],
          "parts": [{ "id": "POL-AC-001_smt", "name": "statement", "prose": "..." }]
        },
        {
          "id": "POL-AC-002",
          "title": "Systems shall enforce session timeouts...",
          "props": [
            { "name": "modality", "value": "normative" }
          ],
          "parts": [...]
        },
        {
          "id": "POL-AC-003",
          "title": "Organizations should implement logging...",
          "props": [
            { "name": "modality", "value": "advisory" }
          ],
          "parts": [...]
        },
        {
          "id": "POL-AC-004",
          "title": "Periodic access reviews may be conducted...",
          "props": [
            { "name": "modality", "value": "advisory" }
          ],
          "parts": [...]
        },
        {
          "id": "POL-AC-005",
          "title": "Encrypt all data at rest...",
          "props": [
            { "name": "modality", "value": "normative" }
          ],
          "parts": [...]
        }
      ]
    }]
  }
}
```

> Note: "Encrypt all data at rest" has no RFC 2119 verb. It defaults to `normative` with a warning emitted to stderr.

### Stderr Output (warnings)

```
WARN forge::parse::modality: Requirement at line 6 has no modality verb; defaulting to normative (source: "Encrypt all data at rest using approved algorithms.")
```

## Usage in Code (Programmatic API)

```rust
use forge::parse::modality::annotate_modalities;
use forge::model::{Modality, PolicyDocument};

// After running the standard pipeline stages...
let doc_with_citations: PolicyDocument = /* ... */;

// Step 7c: Annotate modalities
let doc = annotate_modalities(doc_with_citations)?;

// All requirements now have a modality
for section in &doc.sections {
    for req in &section.requirements {
        match req.modality {
            Some(Modality::Normative) => {
                println!("MANDATORY: {}", req.text);
            }
            Some(Modality::Advisory) => {
                println!("recommended: {}", req.text);
            }
            None => unreachable!("annotate_modalities guarantees Some"),
        }
    }
}
```

---

## Detection Logic Quick Reference

| Requirement Text | Result | Reason |
|-----------------|--------|--------|
| "Systems must enforce MFA" | `Normative` | "must" matched |
| "Systems MUST enforce MFA" | `Normative` | Case-insensitive: "MUST" matched |
| "Organizations shall implement..." | `Normative` | "shall" matched |
| "This will be enforced..." | `Normative` | "will" matched |
| "Authentication is required" | `Normative` | "required" matched |
| "Organizations should implement..." | `Advisory` | "should" matched |
| "Review may occur quarterly" | `Advisory` | "may" matched |
| "Encryption is recommended" | `Advisory` | "recommended" matched |
| "This control is optional" | `Advisory` | "optional" matched |
| "Encrypt all data at rest" | `Normative` + warn | Default (no verb) |
| "Must and should both appear" | `Normative` + warn | Conflict; normative wins |
| "You must not share passwords" | `Normative` | "must not" → "must" is normative |
| "Customize your settings" | *(no match)* | "must" not matched — word boundary prevents "custo**must**omize"... actually "custo**m**ize" — correct, no false match |
| "Display results" | *(no match)* | "may" not matched — "dis**may**..." — wait, "dismay" — correct, no false match via `\b` |

---

## False-Positive Prevention Examples

The `\b` word boundary anchor prevents these false matches:

| Text | Verb | Would Match Without `\b`? | Matches With `\b`? |
|------|------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| "customize the settings" | "must" | ❌ No ("custo**m**ize" doesn't contain "must") | ❌ No |
| "dismay the audience" | "may" | ✅ Yes (substring match) | ❌ No (word boundary) |
| "shouldering the burden" | "should" | ✅ Yes (substring match) | ❌ No (word boundary) |
| "required" (standalone) | "required" | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (intended) |
| "May 2026 review" | "may" | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (limitation — accepted per SEC R3) |

## Environment & Build

No new setup required. WI-33 adds no new dependencies:

```bash
# Build
cargo build

# Run all tests (includes WI-33 modality tests)
cargo test

# Check coverage for modality module (target: ≥90%)
cargo tarpaulin --lib -- parse::modality

# Lint
cargo clippy -- -D warnings

# Format check
cargo fmt --check
```
